close_reason: Added new() constructors to all four Mdn*Request/Response types in crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mdn.rs, matching the sibling pattern in submission.rs (Address::new, Envelope::new, EmailSubmission::new) and vacation.rs (VacationResponse::new): required fields are positional args, optionals default to None, extra defaults to empty Map. Added one round-trip-against-spec test (mdn_request_response_constructors_match_spec_minimal_shape) asserting each constructor produces the minimal RFC 9007 §3.1/§3.3 wire shape with no extra keys. Test oracle is hand-written JSON from RFC 9007, not derived from code under test. Tests + clippy clean.
description:
crate-jmap-mail-types/src/mdn.rs defines four request/response types with `#[non_exhaustive]`:

- MdnSendRequest (line 238)
- MdnSendResponse (line 269)
- MdnParseRequest (line 290)
- MdnParseResponse (line 307)

None of the four has an associated `new()` or any other constructor. `#[non_exhaustive]` makes struct-literal syntax unavailable to callers outside this crate (workspace AGENTS.md design rule), so a client crate that needs to construct these for outgoing requests has no API surface to do so.

The sibling `Mdn` (line 200) has `Mdn::new(disposition)` and `Disposition::new(action_mode, sending_mode, type_)`. Every other migrated type in the diff has a `new()` (Address, Envelope, DeliveryStatus, EmailSubmission, Thread, Identity, SearchSnippet, VacationResponse, SieveScript, Mailbox, MailboxRights, Email, EmailAddress, EmailAddressGroup, EmailHeader, EmailBodyValue).

This is a pre-existing condition (the four types existed pre-9c0d34f without constructors), but the extras-preservation migration adds `extra: serde_json::Map` as a new field. Even though `extra` is `#[serde(default)]`, the type still cannot be struct-literal-constructed externally. A consumer who needs to build an `MdnSendRequest` today must either deserialize one from JSON or fall back to `serde_json::Value` and `from_value`.

The MDN gating note: this is all behind `#[cfg(feature="mdn")]` so the impact is limited to consumers who enable the mdn feature. But that's still the case where ergonomics matters most — those consumers want to USE the MDN types.

Fix: add four `new(account_id: Id, ...)` constructors taking only the required fields, defaulting optional fields and `extra` to empty. Pattern is established by sibling types in the same file (see Mdn::new at line 215).

Construction:
- `MdnSendRequest::new(account_id, identity_id, send) -> Self` — send defaults to empty? Or required?
- `MdnSendResponse::new(account_id) -> Self`
- `MdnParseRequest::new(account_id, blob_ids) -> Self`
- `MdnParseResponse::new(account_id) -> Self`

Priority P2 because the gap blocks external client-side construction; pre-existing means it's not strictly a regression from this diff, but the diff is the natural time to close it because the migration touches all four types.
title: MdnSendRequest, MdnSendResponse, MdnParseRequest, MdnParseResponse are non_exhaustive but have no new() constructor — unconstructible externally
